facts.statement: Misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparisons made to induce someone to lapse, surrender, terminate, retain or convert a policy or annuity are prohibited (twisting).
facts.quote: No person shall make any misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of any insurance policies or annuity contracts or insurers for the purpose of inducing, or tending to induce, any person to lapse, forfeit, surrender, terminate, retain, or convert any insurance policy or annuity contract

items.stem: A producer shows a client an incomplete comparison that hides the surrender charges on a new annuity, to persuade her to cash in her current annuity and buy the new one. This is known as:
options: Twisting
Rebating
Defamation
Sliding
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-6 prohibits misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparisons of policies or annuities made to induce someone to surrender one and take out another. This is twisting.

items.stem: New Jersey's prohibition on misleading policy comparisons applies when the comparison is used to induce someone to do which of the following?
options: Increase the face amount of an existing policy
Change the payment mode of an existing policy
Keep or convert a current policy
Add a rider to an existing policy
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-6 covers misleading comparisons made to induce a person to lapse, forfeit, surrender, terminate, retain or convert a policy, not only to replace it.

items.stem: A producer persuades a client to drop her whole life policy and buy a new one from a different insurer, using a comparison that leaves out the new policy's surrender charges. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Rebating
Defamation
Twisting
A permitted replacement
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-6 prohibits incomplete or misleading comparisons made to induce someone to lapse or surrender a policy and take one out in another insurer. That is twisting.

facts.statement: Making false or misleading statements about dividends or surplus previously paid on similar policies is prohibited.
facts.quote: make any false or misleading statement as to the dividends or share of surplus previously paid on similar policies or annuity contracts

items.stem: A producer tells a prospect that the participating policy he is selling "comes from a line of policies that has paid 8% dividends every year for 20 years." Similar policies actually paid between 3% and 5%. Under New Jersey law, the statement is:
options: Permitted, since dividends are not guaranteed
Misrepresentation
Permitted if an illustration is also provided
Twisting
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-3 prohibits false or misleading statements about dividends or surplus previously paid on similar policies.

facts.statement: Using a policy name or title that misrepresents the policy's true nature is prohibited.
facts.quote: use any name or title of any policy or annuity contract or class of policies or annuity contracts misrepresenting the true nature thereof

items.stem: An insurer sells a 10-year term policy under the product name "Lifetime Wealth Builder." Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Misrepresentation of what the product is
Permitted, because product names are marketing
Twisting
Permitted if the policy form says it is term insurance
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-3 prohibits using any name or title of a policy or annuity that misrepresents its true nature.

facts.statement: Rebating includes giving a client any part of the agent's, solicitor's or broker's commission as an inducement.
facts.quote: any rebate of premiums or considerations payable on the contract or of any agent's, solicitor's or broker's commission relating thereto

items.stem: A producer offers to give a new life insurance client half of the producer's commission on the policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Commission splitting, which is legal between licensed persons
Permitted if the client signs a written waiver
An illegal rebate
A permitted marketing allowance
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-13 prohibits giving, as an inducement, any rebate of premiums or of any agent's, solicitor's or broker's commission on the contract.

facts.statement: After a hearing, the commissioner may order a penalty of up to $1,000 per violation, or up to $5,000 per violation if the person knew or reasonably should have known it was a violation.
facts.quote: the commissioner may order payment of a penalty not to exceed $1,000.00 for each and every act or violation unless the person knew or reasonably should have known he was in violation of this chapter, in which case the penalty shall be not more than $5,000.00 for every act or violation

items.stem: After a hearing, the commissioner finds a producer violated New Jersey's life and annuity trade practice rules without knowing, or having reason to know, it was a violation. The maximum penalty per violation is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 caps the penalty at $1,000 for each violation unless the person knew or reasonably should have known it was a violation.

items.stem: If a producer knew or reasonably should have known that the conduct violated New Jersey's life and annuity trade practice rules, the maximum penalty per violation is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 raises the maximum penalty to $5,000 for every violation when the person knew or reasonably should have known it was a violation.

items.stem: After a hearing, a producer is found to have knowingly made three misleading policy comparisons in violation of New Jersey's life trade practice rules. The maximum total penalty is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 allows up to $5,000 for every violation when the person knew or reasonably should have known it was a violation. Three violations come to $15,000.

facts.statement: After finding a violation at a hearing, the commissioner issues an order to cease and desist.
facts.quote: an order requiring such person to cease and desist from engaging in such method of competition, act or practice

items.stem: When the commissioner finds, after a hearing, that a person engaged in a prohibited life or annuity trade practice, the commissioner issues:
options: A desist warning with no penalty possible
An order to cease and desist
An automatic license revocation
A referral for criminal prosecution
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 directs the commissioner, after a hearing and written findings, to issue an order requiring the person to cease and desist from the practice, with any penalty ordered.

facts.statement: Before ordering a stop to a prohibited practice, the commissioner serves a statement of charges and notice of a hearing.
facts.quote: he shall issue and serve upon such person a statement of the charges in that respect and a notice of a hearing thereon

items.stem: Before the commissioner can order a person to stop an unfair life or annuity trade practice, what must the commissioner first serve on that person?
options: A cease and desist order effective immediately
A notice of a hearing only
A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
A civil complaint filed in Superior Court
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 requires the commissioner to serve a statement of the charges and a notice of a hearing before any cease and desist order or penalty.

facts.statement: Before starting a life insurance sales presentation, the agent must say that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and give the full name of the insurer represented.
facts.quote: prior to commencing a life insurance sales presentation, that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and the full name of the insurer the agent is representing

items.stem: Under New Jersey's life insurance disclosure rules, what must an agent tell a prospect before starting a life insurance sales presentation?
options: His commission rate on the proposed policy
His license number and its expiration date
The names of every insurer that has appointed him
That he sells life insurance, and which company he represents
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.4(b)-(c) requires the agent to say, prior to commencing a life insurance sales presentation, that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and to give the full name of the insurer.

facts.statement: A producer may not use titles like financial planner or investment advisor to imply an advisory business with compensation unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case.
facts.quote: in such a way as to imply that he or she is primarily engaged in an advisory business in which compensation is unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case

items.stem: A New Jersey life producer paid entirely by commissions on policy sales uses business cards reading "Financial Consultant" and describes his business as an advisory practice. He holds no planning designation. Under New Jersey rules, this is:
options: Prohibited, because it implies his pay is unrelated to sales
Permitted, since producers who discuss finances may use the title
Permitted, if he also holds a securities license
Permitted, if the title also appears on the application
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.4(b)-(c) bars using terms such as financial planner or financial counseling to imply an advisory business with compensation unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case.

facts.statement: Failing to deliver a required Buyer's Guide, policy summary or illustration is an omission that misrepresents the policy and can bring Unfair Trade Practices Act penalties.
facts.quote: shall constitute an omission that misrepresents the benefits, advantages, conditions or terms of an insurance policy

items.stem: Under New Jersey's life insurance disclosure rules, a producer's failure to deliver a required Buyer's Guide is treated as:
options: A clerical error with no penalty
An omission that misrepresents the policy
A breach of contract only
A matter for the insured to raise in court
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.5 treats failure to deliver a required Buyer's Guide, policy summary, illustration or policy data as an omission that misrepresents the policy, subject to Unfair Trade Practices Act penalties.

facts.statement: When using an illustration, a producer may not describe a plan of using non-guaranteed elements to pay future premiums as a 'vanishing premium.'
facts.quote: Use the term "vanish" or "vanishing premium," or a similar term that implies the policy becomes paid up

items.stem: Under New Jersey's life insurance illustration rules, which term may a producer NOT use to describe a plan in which future dividends pay part of the premiums?
options: Vanishing premium
Premium offset
Dividend option
Paid-up additions
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.4(a)-(b) bars using "vanish," "vanishing premium" or a similar term that implies the policy becomes paid up to describe using non-guaranteed elements to pay part of future premiums.
items.retired: Answerable by common sense or ethics instinct.

facts.statement: If a policy is applied for as illustrated, a signed copy of the illustration goes to the insurer with the application, and a copy to the applicant.
facts.quote: a copy of that illustration, signed in accordance with these rules, shall be submitted to the insurer at the time of policy application

items.stem: A producer uses a basic illustration, and the client applies for the policy exactly as illustrated. Under New Jersey rules, when must the signed illustration be submitted to the insurer?
options: When the policy is delivered
Along with the application
Within 30 days after issue
Only if the insurer requests it
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires a signed copy of the illustration to be submitted to the insurer at the time of application when the policy is applied for as illustrated, with a copy to the applicant.

facts.statement: If the policy is issued other than as applied for, a 'Revised Illustration' must be sent with the policy and signed by the owner and producer no later than delivery.
facts.quote: shall be labeled "Revised Illustration" and shall be signed and dated by the applicant or policy owner and producer

items.stem: A client applied for a policy as illustrated, but the insurer issues it at a higher rating class. Under New Jersey rules, what must accompany the policy?
options: An amended application signed by the client
A rating letter, with no new illustration
A revised illustration, signed by delivery
The original illustration, marked with the new premium
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires a revised basic illustration labeled "Revised Illustration," conforming to the policy as issued, sent with the policy and signed by the owner and producer no later than delivery.

facts.statement: If no illustration is used, the producer must certify that in writing on a form provided by the insurer.
facts.quote: the producer or representative shall certify to that effect in writing on a form provided by the insurer

items.stem: A producer sells a life policy that is marketed with illustrations but shows the client no illustration at all. Under New Jersey rules, the producer must:
options: Do nothing, since showing illustrations is optional
Mail the client an illustration within 30 days
Get the commissioner's approval for the sale
Sign a statement on the company's form saying none was shown
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires the producer to certify in writing, on a form provided by the insurer, that no illustration was used.

facts.statement: Signed illustrations and certifications must be kept by the insurer until three years after the policy is no longer in force.
facts.quote: shall be retained by the insurer until three years after the policy is no longer in force

items.stem: How long must a New Jersey insurer keep a policy's signed illustration?
options: Until three years after the policy is no longer in force
One year after issue
Five years after issue
Until the policy's next anniversary
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires the insurer to retain signed illustrations and related certifications until three years after the policy is no longer in force.

facts.statement: A producer may not use a self-conferred, nonexistent, or unearned senior-specific certification or designation to imply special expertise with seniors.
facts.quote: The use of a nonexistent or self-conferred certification or professional designation

items.stem: A producer prints "Certified Senior Retirement Advisor" on her cards. She created the title herself and completed no course. Under New Jersey rules, this is:
options: Allowed, since it describes her client base
Prohibited, since she gave herself the title
Allowed, if she has ten years of experience
Prohibited, unless she also sells annuities
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-60.3(a),(c) bars using a nonexistent or self-conferred certification or designation to imply special expertise in advising seniors.
items.retired: Answerable by common sense or ethics instinct.
